note: The 12 §1.1 tree-digest convention, as data. Read IN PLACE by `tools/ci/tests/test_check_release_reproducibility.py` and by `app/tests/release/repro-manifest.test.ts`, so the Python consumer and the TypeScript producer cannot drift apart about what a tree hash is. A divergence turns one of them red.
convention: sha256 over `path \0 <file sha256> \n` for every path, sorted

cases.name: one file
cases.why: the smallest map that certifies anything

cases.name: a realistic release
cases.why: dist/ and release-out/ under one digest, as the manifest carries them

cases.name: insertion order does not matter
cases.why: the same three entries written in reverse; the digest sorts, so it must equal the case above

cases.name: a rename is not reproduced
cases.why: identical bytes under a different path — every file digest matches the case above and the tree digest MUST NOT

refusals.name: an empty tree
refusals.why: two builds that emitted nothing agree on the digest of nothing; that must never read as a reproduction

refusals.name: a digest that is not one
refusals.why: the map would not be what it claims and the digest would certify it anyway

refusals.name: a digest of the wrong length
refusals.why: 63 hex characters is a truncated sha256, which is a comparison that can never match
